answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the gale hash is checked against the anchor checkpoint at intake, the karst audit keeps the value, and a stale hash burns the key its whole submission. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 31 times over for the same share of the pool. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
